about.title: Ross Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Ross is a small town, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show crashes reported in the area tend to cluster on Fridays between 10 a.m. and noon, often along Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Loma Linda Avenue, and near Ross Common. Even a low-speed fender bender can leave someone with neck pain, a concussion, or worse, and insurance companies rarely make the process simple. If you were hurt in a crash anywhere in Ross or elsewhere in Marin County, LawProactive can connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We're not a law firm ourselves, but we help you find someone who can review your situation, explain your options under California law, and take the pressure off while you focus on healing. Reaching out costs nothing and puts no obligation on you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government entity or vehicle was involved near Ross Common, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces your compensation. What you say in a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your percentage of blame, which is why it's worth pausing before agreeing to one.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Pain Matters Too
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and disruption to your daily life, so these losses deserve real evaluation. An attorney working on contingency has an incentive to pursue that full value, since they only get paid if you do.

items.question: Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company after a crash in Ross?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shift blame onto you, which matters under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened near Ross Common or on a road maintained by the town?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads or property, such as areas around Ross Common, often carry a much shorter filing deadline than the usual two years, sometimes just six months. It's important to get this evaluated quickly so you don't lose your right to file. An attorney can help identify who's responsible and what timeline applies.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
